answer: Reverse-dependency inlet access. Each identity may draw resources only through an inlet keyed to a distinct upstream dependency graph; cloning forces the attacker to replicate that full graph per clone, so cost scales linearly with sybil count rather than staying flat. Honest agents reuse one earned graph, a cheap haven from duplication. A shared-source echo flags clusters at admission, and cloned graphs lose access to scarce upstream slots, making N fakes cost roughly N times an honest identity's setup.
